newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine labor talks end with pledge to reconvene.
newsitem.headline: Argentine labor talks end with pledge to reconvene.

text.p: Argentine government officials, trade unionists and business leaders on Thursday emerged from three-way talks on solving the country's job crisis with little comment, expect to say they committed to further discussions on ways to fight unemployment.

"We will carry on discussing any suggestion to try to solve the problem which worries our society most -- rampant unemployment," said Jorge Blanco Villegas of the powerful Argentine Industrial Union employers' association.

The leader of Argentina's main CGT labor confederation, Rodolfo Daer, said three-way talks would resume next week with an open agenda and the discussions could touch on other economic issues, such as tax evasion.

The government hopes the meetings will soothe tensions between government, unions and business that escalated after President Carlos Menem signed three decrees in December to reform Argentina's labor laws and reduce the unions' grip on pay negotiations.

Unions responded by launching a general strike on December 26. Two weeks ago, the government pledged to stop pushing its labor reform program by means of presidential decree, and unions agreed to return to the negotiating table.
